title: Analysing Differences in Persuasive Language in LLM-Generated Text: Uncovering Stereotypical Gender Patterns

bias_targets.methodology: Using pairwise prompt instructions that vary only the recipient's gender identifier (e.g., male vs. female) to generate persuasive messages and arguments. An LLM-as-judge setup then evaluates the responses across 19 categories of persuasive language (such as agentic vs. communal traits, and emotional vs. logical appeals) to quantify stereotypical stylistic differences.

Prompting models to generate persuasive texts in 16 different languages (acting as the treatment variable) to evaluate cross-lingual differences in persuasive style. An LLM-as-judge assesses pairwise differences across languages, measuring variations in dimensions like formality, politeness, and overall persuasive strategies (e.g., comparing Japanese, English, and German).
